# Uniques

_Generated from PoB tree data `3.29`. Regenerate after any data update - this script
rebuilds `uniques.db` too._

A unique may be designed around IF AND ONLY IF it has a row in `data/uniques.db`.
Memory-sourced names are hypotheses - one query settles existence and legality
together; zero rows, for any reason, means no. The db holds only legal content:
unobtainable uniques (181 of 1325) and legacy-only mod lines are excluded at
generation - never filter for legality yourself. The sections after the schema
document traps ON obtainable items.

## Querying uniques.db

Run `sqlite3` with paths from the repo root (from `src/`, prefix `../`). Double any
apostrophe inside SQL strings: `name='Watcher''s Eye'`.

- `uniques(id, name, base, type, subtype, league, source, req_level, req_str,
  req_dex, req_int)` - one row per name per base (Grand Spectrum: one per jewel
  colour); a base that differs by variant is " | "-joined inside `base`.
- `mods(id, unique_id, scope, line, template, variant, unsupported)` -
  scope `implicit|explicit|buff|enchant`; `line` keeps ranges (`+(10-77)% to ...`);
  `template` is the line with every number/range as `#` - LIKE-match on it, not on
  `line`; `variant` is " | "-joined names of the (non-legacy) variants carrying the
  line, NULL = unconditional; `unsupported=1` = PoB cannot calculate the line, it
  has no effect in a build.
- `mod_values(mod_id, ord, min, max)` - a line's numbers in reading order; fixed
  values have min = max. Numeric criteria go here, never regex on `line`.
- `foulborn_swaps(unique_id, replaces, replacement)` - see Foulborn below.
- `meta(key, value)` - `tree_version`, `generated_at`.

Canonical queries:

```sh
DB=.claude/skills/cook/data/uniques.db
# existence + slot - zero rows means DO NOT USE, whatever the reason
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT id, base, type, req_level FROM uniques WHERE name='Seven Teachings';"
# full mod listing for one item
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT m.scope, m.line, m.variant, m.unsupported FROM mods m
  JOIN uniques u ON u.id=m.unique_id WHERE u.name='Seven Teachings';"
# criteria search: crit multi roll >= 50 wearable before level 60
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT u.name, u.req_level, m.line FROM mods m
  JOIN uniques u ON u.id=m.unique_id JOIN mod_values v ON v.mod_id=m.id AND v.ord=1
  WHERE m.template LIKE '%to Critical Strike Multiplier%' AND v.max>=50 AND u.req_level<60;"
```

## Variants

662 obtainable uniques carry at least one legacy variant - a roll that existed before
some patch and cannot be obtained now. The db already excludes legacy-only lines and
names the surviving rolls in `mods.variant`; this section is about AUTHORING the item
into a build.

`Item.lua:1496` defaults an item to its **last** variant:
`self.variant = m_min(#self.variantList, self.variant or #self.variantList)`. Raw item
text can pin any variant with a `Selected Variant:` line, and PoB keeps a legacy pick
without complaint - so always read back the variant you actually got.

### Per-mod variant items

These encode one variant per possible mod **roll** rather than one per item version -
Watcher's Eye has 106, one per aura mod - and several can be selected at once through
`variantAlt1..5`. "Use the last variant" is meaningless here: it just picks the last
aura in the list. A legacy roll sits directly beside its replacement under a name that
says so - same wording, nerfed numbers - so the name is what identifies the roll (query
`mods.variant` for the legal ones). Every variant's lines live in the item text at
once, selected or not, which is the trap: read them through
`Item:CheckModLineVariant` or you will judge a mod the item does not have.
`validate.lua` does both.

## Foulborn

Not a league mechanic - permanent, and roughly a year older than 3.29.

A Foulborn unique **replaces** one of its normal mods with a mutated counterpart. It
is not an extra mod, and you pick which one is replaced: 240 obtainable uniques offer
334 possible swaps between them, all in `foulborn_swaps`:

```sh
sqlite3 $DB "SELECT f.replaces, f.replacement FROM foulborn_swaps f
  JOIN uniques u ON u.id=f.unique_id WHERE u.name='Abyssus';"
```

To put one in a build spec, tag the replacement line `{mutated}` in the item's raw
text. The `Foulborn ` name prefix is derived from that tag (`Item.lua:1564`), so
writing it yourself does nothing.

`Might of the Meek` is excluded: its transformation changes a radius rather than a
mod line, which PoB cannot represent (`Item.lua:999`).
